titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§202–203: The Ninety-Five Thousands, and Shigi-Qutuqu
about: Chinggis is raised to Qan in the Tiger year, and the roll of the ninety-five thousand-commanders he appointed is read out name by name. Then Shigi-Qutuqu, sent to fetch the lords, instead pleads for his own reward, recalling that he grew up at Chinggis's threshold; Chinggis makes him supreme judge, orders the shares and judgments of the whole people to be written in a Blue Register after consulting him, and warns that no one may alter what is written in it.

sentences.t: Tedüi hisgei toγ̇urγatu ulus-i šidurγudγažu bars žil Onan-(n)u teriġün-e qurižu
sentences.l: Those felt tent-skirt-having people (obj.) having-made-straight, tiger year, Onan's head-at gathering,
sentences.i: When they had set in order those people of the felt tents, they gathered in the Tiger year at the source of the Onan,
sentences.n: Begins the account of the assembly of 1206 (the Tiger year, by the usual reckoning) and is the first half of one converb chain, cut in two here (the second half runs from jesün to ögbe). Tedüi hisgei toγ̇urγatu ulus-i is 'those felt-and-tent-skirt-having people (object)': -tu is the possessive 'having' (Ming 有的), and toγ̇urγa is the skirt of the felt tent (帳裙). šidurγudγažu is a causative converb, Ming 敎直了着 'having caused (them) to be straight'; I read it as 'set in order' (a causative, not a passive), but its stem and suffixes are uncertain. No subject is stated. Chinggis is the one who receives the title in the next unit, so the actors are evidently the assembled chiefs, and I write 'they'. Onan-(n)u: the (n) is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: those, so many (here a pronoun) [那些]
tent-skirt, the lower wall of the tent [帳裙]
to be straight, upright (stem uncertain; Ming 直) [敎直了着]
the Onon, the river of Chinggis's homeland [河名]

sentences.t: jesün költü čaγaγ̇an tuγ baiγ̇ulγ̇ad Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a qān nere tende ögbe.
sentences.l: Nine foot-having white banner having-set-up, to Chinggis Qaγan Qān name there gave.
sentences.i: They raised the nine-footed white banner and there gave Chinggis Qahan the name of Qan.
sentences.n: Second half of the chain. költü is köl 'foot, leg' + -tü 'having' (Ming 腳有的): a banner 'nine-footed', perhaps with nine tails or points; the Ming say no more. tuγ is the standard (Ming 旄纛). baiγ̇ulγ̇ad is baiγ̇ul- 'set up' + -γ̇ad 'having'. Qaγan-(n)a is the dative-locative 'to' (Ming 行), so Chinggis is the one given the name, not the giver; the subject of ögbe is still unstated. qān nere is 'the name Qan' (nere is 'name' and also 'title, rank'): the short title, which Shiratori prints qān and `i` writes 'Qan', against Qaγan, 'Qahan'.

morph.gloss: to set up, make stand (from bai- 'stand') [立了]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
qan, ruler (the short title Qan) [皇帝]

sentences.t: Muqali-da Γuowaṅ nere tende-kü ögbe.
sentences.l: To Muqali, Guowang name there also gave.
sentences.i: To Muqali they also gave there the title of Guowang.
sentences.n: Γuowaṅ is not Mongolian: the characters 國王 are the Chinese title guowang, 'prince of the state', written in its own characters (the Ming mark it 官名, 'official title'). nere here is 'title'. kü 'also, indeed' (Ming 也) follows tende 'there'.

morph.gloss: Guowang, the Chinese title 國王 'prince of the state' (written in its own characters) [(官名)]

sentences.t: Žebe-ji Naiman-(n)u Küčülüg Qān-i nekeġülün tende kü čaγ̇uraγ̇ulba.
sentences.l: Jebe (obj.), Naiman's Küčülüg Qān (obj.) causing-to-pursue, there also made-to-go-out-on-campaign.
sentences.i: Jebe was likewise sent out there on campaign, to pursue Küchülüg Qan of the Naiman.
sentences.n: Both Žebe-ji and Qān-i carry the accusative (-ji after a vowel, -i after a consonant; Ming 行 on each). nekeġülün is a causative converb, 'causing to pursue' (Ming 敎襲着, 'cause to attack'; 'pursue' follows the glossary's reading of neke-), and čaγ̇uraγ̇ulba a causative, 'sent out on campaign' (the stem čaγ̇ura- is inferred from the Ming 征). Küčülüg Qān is the Naiman prince; Qān is the short title again (Ming 皇帝). tende kü, 'there also', I render 'likewise'.

morph.gloss: qan, ruler (short form beside qaγan) [(皇帝)]
to go out on campaign (stem inferred from the Ming 征) [敎征了]

sentences.t: Moṅγolžin ulus-i žibšijerün baražu
sentences.l: Moṅγolžin people (obj.) arranging, having-finished.
sentences.i: Having finished putting the Mongol people in order,
sentences.n: Moṅγolžin: the Ming gloss it 達達 'Tatars', as they gloss Monγol elsewhere; I cannot analyse the ending -žin, so it is kept whole and read 'the Mongols'. žibšije- is 'to put in order, arrange' (Ming 整治); baražu 'finishing, being used up' closes the converb chain before the decree.

morph.gloss: the Mongols (a form in -žin; analysis uncertain) [達達]
to put in order, arrange [整治]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan decree being-when:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: žarliγ bolurun is the formula 'issued a decree' (Ming 聖旨 做, 'the edict made'), -urun the converb of time. The colon is Shiratori's; the decree itself opens at the next word, whose opening quotation mark he prints.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Ulus baiγ̇ululčan jabulduγsad-ta
sentences.l: Realm jointly-establishing, to the together-having-gone,
sentences.i: “To those who went together and jointly founded the realm,
sentences.n: The decree is one long sentence, cut here into three units (42–44, 45–49, 50–55). Shiratori's opening quote mark stands on Ulus, and his closing mark on ügülesü (52). baiγ̇ululčan is baiγ̇ul- 'establish' + -lča- 'jointly' (Ming 共) + the converb -n. jabulduγsad-ta is jabu- 'go' + -ldu- 'together' (Ming 共) + the past participle -γsad (plural; Ming 來的每) + the dative -ta (行): 'to those who had gone together'. I take them to be the companions of the early years, but the words do not say so.

sentences.t: miṅγan minγalažu miṅγad-un nojad tüšižü
sentences.l: A thousand, thousand-making, thousands' lords appointing,
sentences.i: having formed thousands and appointed lords over the thousands,
sentences.n: miṅγan 'thousand' is the military and administrative unit of a thousand households or men. minγalažu is miṅγala- 'make into a thousand' (Ming 千做着). miṅγad-un is miṅγan + plural -d + genitive -un (Ming 千(戶)的): 'of the thousands', and with nojad 'lords' (noyan + -d) the possessor stands first: 'thousands' lords'. tüšižü 'appointing, entrusting' (Ming 委付着) ends the converb chain.

morph.gloss: to form into thousands (from miṅγan) [千做着]

sentences.t: sojurγal üge ügülesü" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Favour word let-me-speak,” saying, decree it-became.
sentences.i: let me speak a word of favour.” So it was decreed.
sentences.n: sojurγal is 'favour, grace' (Ming 恩賜), here a spoken grant: sojurγal üge 'word of favour'. ügülesü is ügüle- 'speak' + the optative -sü, 'let me say' (Ming 說我, 'I will say'); Shiratori's closing quote mark is printed on it, and keġen 'saying' closes the quotation. žarliγ bolba, 'it became a decree' (Ming 聖旨做了), says the speech was issued as a decree.

morph.gloss: favour, grace, bounty (from sojurγa- 'to show favour') [恩賜]

sentences.t: Miṅγad-un nojad tüšin nereidürün
sentences.l: Thousands' lords appointing, naming-when,
sentences.i: When the lords of the thousands were appointed and named:
sentences.n: What follows is the roll of the ninety-five thousand-commanders. The Ming gloss every name only 人名 'a man's name', so I identify none of them beyond the spelling. nereidürün is nereidü- 'to name' (from nere 'name'; Ming 名分時, 'when giving rank') + -rün 'when'. As before, tüšin is the converb of tüši- 'appoint'.

morph.gloss: to name, give a name or rank (from nere 'name') [名分時]

sentences.t: Müṅlig Ečige, Boγ̇orču, Muqali-Guowaṅ, Qorči, Ilügei, Žürčedei, Qunan, Qubilai, Želme, Tüge, Degei,
sentences.l: Müṅlig Ečige, Boγ̇orču, Muqali-Guowaṅ, Qorči, Ilügei, Žürčedei, Qunan, Qubilai, Želme, Tüge, Degei,
sentences.i: Father Münlig, Bo'orchu, Muqali Guowang, Qorchi, Ilügei, Jürchedei, Qunan, Qubilai, Jelme, Tüge, Degei,
sentences.n: The roll of names begins. Müṅlig is followed by ečige 'father' (Ming 父), and the house rendering is 'Father Münlig'. Muqali-Guowaṅ is Muqali with his Chinese title (see the third unit above). The Ming give each name only 人名; I give Shiratori's spelling in `l` and a plain English spelling in `i`. The list is one list, cut in runs of about a dozen for the screen.

morph.gloss: Muqali Guowang, Muqali with his title Guowang 'prince of the state', a man's name [人名]

sentences.t: Tolon, Öṅgür, Čülgetei, Boroγul, Šigi-Qutuqu, Küčü, Kököčü, Qorγosun, Hüsün, Huildar, Šilügei, Žetei,

sentences.i: Tolon, Önggür, Chülgetei, Boroqul, Shigi-Qutuqu, Küchü, Kököchü, Qorqosun, Hüsün, Quildar, Shilügei, Jetei,
sentences.n: The roll continues. Šigi-Qutuqu, the man of the second half of this part, is here only a name in the roll. Küčü and Hüsün are also ordinary words ('strength', 'hair, down'), used as names.

morph.gloss: Küchü, a man's name (küčü 'strength' used as a name) [人名]
Hüsün, a man's name (hüsün 'hair, down' used as a name) [人名]

Küchügür, a man's name (küčügür 'field-mouse', uncertain, used as a name) [人名]

sentences.t: Oronartai, Dair, Müge, Bužir, Müṅgüġür, Doloγ̇adai, Bögen, Qudus, Maral, Žebke, Juruγan, Kökö,
sentences.l: Oronartai, Dair, Müge, Bužir, Müṅgüġür, Doloγ̇adai, Bögen, Qudus, Maral, Žebke, Juruγan, Kökö,
sentences.i: Oronartai, Dair, Müge, Bujir, Münggügür, Dolo'adai, Bögen, Qudus, Maral, Jebke, Juruqan, Kökö,
sentences.n: The roll continues. Dair elsewhere is a horse's name; here the Ming say 人名. Maral ('hind') and Kökö ('blue') are also words used as names.

morph.gloss: Maral, a man's name (maral 'hind' used as a name) [人名]
Kökö, a man's name (kökö 'blue' used as a name) [人名]

sentences.t: Žebe, Udutai, Bala-Čerbi, Kete, Sübeġetei, Müṅkö, Qalža, Qurčaqus, Kögi, Badai, Kišiliγ, Ketei,
sentences.l: Žebe, Udutai, Bala-Čerbi, Kete, Sübeġetei, Müṅkö, Qalža, Qurčaqus, Kögi, Badai, Kišiliγ, Ketei,

sentences.n: The roll continues. This Žebe is presumably the man sent against Küčülüg above (same spelling; the Ming say only 人名). Kete is also a word, 'fire-steel' (Ming 火鎌), here a name.

morph.gloss: Kete, a man's name (kete 'fire-steel' used as a name) [人名]

sentences.n: The roll continues. Daγ̇un is also 'sound, voice'.

morph.gloss: Da'un, a man's name (daγ̇un 'sound, voice' used as a name) [人名]

sentences.t: Alči, Tosaγa, Tuṅγuidai, Tobuqa, Ažinai, Tüideger, Sečeġür, Žeder, Olar-Küregen, Kiṅgijadai,
sentences.l: Alči, Tosaγa, Tuṅγuidai, Tobuqa, Ažinai, Tüideger, Sečeġür, Žeder, Olar-Küregen, Kiṅgijadai,
sentences.i: Alchi, Tosaqa, Tungquidai, Tobuqa, Ajinai, Tüideger, Sechegür, Jeder, Olar Küregen, Kinggijadai,

Asiq Küregen, a man's name [人名]
Qadai Küregen, a man's name [人名]
Chikü Küregen, a man's name [人名]
Alchi Küregen, a man's name [人名]

sentences.t: γurban miṅγad Uṅgirad Butu-Küregen,
sentences.l: Three thousands, Uṅgirad: Butu-Küregen,
sentences.i: three thousands of the Ongirad: Butu Küregen;
sentences.n: The roll turns from single men to whole peoples. γurban miṅγad is 'three thousands' (miṅγad, Ming 千(每), is miṅγan + plural -d). The Ming give Uṅgirad 種名 'name of a people' and Butu-Küregen 人名, side by side; I read the three thousands as the Ongirad's and Butu Küregen as their lord, but the Ming do not join them, so the link is my reading.

morph.gloss: the Ongirad (Shiratori's spelling Uṅgirad), a people [種名]
Butu Küregen, a man's name [人名]

sentences.t: qojar miṅγad Ikires, Öṅgüd-ü, Alaqu-Šidigid, Quri-Küregen,
sentences.l: Two thousands, Ikires, Öṅgüd's Alaqu-Šidigid, Quri-Küregen,
sentences.i: two thousands of the Ikires; of the Önggüd, Alaqu-Shidigid, Quri Küregen;
sentences.n: As in the previous unit, the Ming set the peoples and men side by side without joining them, so the grouping is mine. Öṅgüd-ü is the Önggüd + genitive -ü, 'the Önggüd's' (Ming 種名 only; the Han 汪古敦 ends in 敦, so -ün may be meant, but I keep Shiratori's -ü). Whether Alaqu-Šidigid and Quri-Küregen are two men, as the Ming gloss them (each 人名), or one man's name, as Alaqush-Digit-Quri in §§182–185, I cannot decide, and I keep the Ming's two. The same phrase Öṅgüd-ü Alaqu-Šidigid-Quri stands in §182 as one name, which tilts me toward one man here too (Shiratori's comma and the added -Küregen notwithstanding).

morph.gloss: Quri Küregen, a man's name [人名]

sentences.t: tabun miṅγad Öṅgüd,
sentences.l: Five thousands, Öṅgüd,
sentences.i: and five thousands of the Önggüd,
sentences.n: Closes the run of peoples: tabun miṅγad 'five thousands' (Ming 五千(每)) and Öṅgüd, a people (Ming 種名). It is not clear whether these five thousands are a further body or the Önggüd of the line before; I take them as the Önggüd's own.

sentences.t: hoi-in irgen-eče aṅgida Monγol ulus-un miṅγad-un nojad-i
sentences.l: Forest's peoples-from besides, Monγol people's thousands' lords (obj.),
sentences.i: Apart from the forest peoples, the lords of the thousands of the Mongol people
sentences.n: hoi-in irgen is 'the forest's people' (Ming 林的百姓), the forest peoples; aṅgida with the ablative -eče (irgen-eče) is 'apart from'. The sentence runs on into the next unit, where Chinggis's naming finishes it. I take Monγol ulus-un as 'of the Mongol people' (Ming 達達百姓的; ulus is glossed 百姓 'people', as in Moṅγolžin ulus-i above). nojad-i is nojan + plural -d + accusative -i.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)u nereidügsen jeren tabun miṅγad-un nojad bolba.
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan's named ninety five thousands' lords became.
sentences.i: whom Chinggis Qahan named became the ninety-five lords of thousands.
sentences.n: nereidügsen is nereidü- 'to name' + the past participle -gsen (Ming 提名來的), 'the named', agreeing with the object of the previous unit. jeren tabun is 'ninety five', and bolba 'became' closes the sentence and the section.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to name, give a name or rank (from nere 'name') [提名來的]

sentences.t: Küreged-lüġe nigen-e basa Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: Sons-in-law-with in-one-place, again Čiṅgis Qaγan decree being-when:
sentences.i: Again, in one place together with the sons-in-law, Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: The first words of §203. Küreged-lüġe is küregen 'son-in-law' (Ming 駙馬) + plural -d + comitative -lüġe 'with'; nigen-e is 'in one place, together' (Ming 一處). I take the pair as 'assembled together with the sons-in-law'; the Ming leave it at 一同一處, 'together, in one place'. žarliγ bolurun is the decree formula as in §202.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Ede nereidügsed jeren tabun miṅγad-un nojad-i miṅγan tüšiġed bürün
sentences.l: These named ninety five thousands' lords (obj.), thousand having-appointed, being,
sentences.i: Having set these ninety-five named lords of thousands each over a thousand,
sentences.n: Shiratori prints an opening quote mark on Ede that is never closed before the next opening mark (Tusatan-a, 198). Chinggis is named again at 194, so these words are unlikely to be his speech; I read them as narration, supply no quote mark, and treat the colon before them as the formula only. The sense is circumstantial: the lords have been named and set over thousands. nereidügsed is nereidü- 'to name' + the past participle -gsed (plural) (Ming 提名了的每); tüšiġed 'having appointed' (Ming 委付了); bürün 'being' (Ming 有着).

morph.gloss: to name, give a name or rank (from nere 'name') [提 名了的(每)]

sentences.t: tere dotora Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: That among, Čiṅgis Qaγan decree being-when:
sentences.i: among them Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: tere dotora 'among that', i.e. among these lords. The formula žarliγ bolurun repeats from the first unit of the section; the decree it introduces is the next unit.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Tusatan-a sojurγal ögsü" keġen
sentences.l: To the service-having, favour let-me-give,” saying,
sentences.i: “To those who have rendered service, let me give favour,” he said,
sentences.n: Opening quote on Tusatan-a is Shiratori's; his closing mark is on ögsü. tusatan-a is tusa 'service, benefit' (Ming 恩) + -tan 'those having' + the dative-locative -a: 'to the ones with service' (`i` 'those who have rendered service' puts the possession as a verb; 'good' is not in the words). ögsü is ög- 'give' + the optative -sü, 'let me give'. The speech continues in the next unit: keġen 'saying' is followed by a second, shorter speech.

morph.gloss: favour, grace, bounty (from sojurγa- 'to show favour') [恩賜]

sentences.t: "Boγ̇orču, Muqali teriġüten nojad-i iretügei" keġeküi-dür
sentences.l: “Boγ̇orču, Muqali and-the-headed nobles (obj.) let-(them)-be-made-to-come,” saying-when,
sentences.i: and when he said, “Have the lords come, Bo'orchu, Muqali and the others,”
sentences.n: A second quotation, opened by Shiratori on Boγ̇orču and closed on iretügei. teriġüten is teriġü 'head' + the plural possessive -ten, 'those having a head, the headed ones' (Ming 等項, 'and the like'); the Ming 項 may rather be 'item'. nojad-i is accusative, so iretügei is more 'have them come' than 'let them come'. keġeküi-dür is keġe- 'say' + the participle -küi + dative-locative -dür, 'at the saying, when' (Ming 說的 時).

morph.gloss: to come; with an accusative object, 'have come, summon' [敎來者︀]

sentences.t: ger dotora Šigi-Qutuqu büleġe.
sentences.l: House inside, Šigi-Qutuqu there-was.
sentences.i: Shigi-Qutuqu was inside the tent.
sentences.n: ger is 'house, tent' (Ming 房, here 'room, house'); I say 'tent'. büleġe is bü- 'be' + the past narrative -leġe, 'there was' (Ming 有來). The subject Šigi-Qutuqu is the man who speaks in the rest of the section; the Ming mark him 人名 only.

sentences.t: "Urira od" keġen
sentences.l: “To call go,” saying.
sentences.i: “Go and call them,” he said.
sentences.n: urira is uri- 'call' + -ra, the converb of purpose (Ming 喚, 'in order to call'); od is the bare stem of od- 'go', the imperative. The speaker is not named; given what follows it is Chinggis (or another high speaker) sending Shigi-Qutuqu to fetch the lords just named.

sentences.t: Šigi-Qutuqu-da ügüleġesü Šigi-Qutuqu ügülerün:
sentences.l: Šigi-Qutuqu-to when-he-spoke, Šigi-Qutuqu saying:
sentences.i: When this was said to Shigi-Qutuqu, Shigi-Qutuqu said:
sentences.n: ügüleġesü is ügüle- 'speak' + the conditional converb -ġesü, 'if, when (one) speaks' (Ming 說呵); its subject is the unnamed speaker. The two Šigi-Qutuqu are the addressee (-da, 'to') and the new speaker; the colon introduces his long speech, which Shiratori opens at the next unit.

sentences.t: "Boγ̇orču, Muqali-tan ken-eče hüleġü tusa kileġe.
sentences.l: “Boγ̇orču, Muqali and-the-others, than-whom more service did?
sentences.i: “Than whom did Bo'orchu, Muqali and the others do more service?
sentences.n: Šigi-Qutuqu's speech, a long complaint, runs from here to ögümü (286). It opens with rhetorical questions, which is how I read them: ken-eče, 'than whom' (ablative, 'from'; Ming 誰行), hüleġü 'more' (Ming 多), tusa 'service, benefit' (Ming 恩). The implied answer is perhaps 'than me', but that is my reading. kileġe is the past narrative of ki- 'to do' (Ming 做; the stem the glossary already carries in kibe, kižü). muqali-tan: -tan 'and the like' (Ming 等).

morph.gloss: to do, make (as in kižü, kibe) [做來]

sentences.t: Ken-eče hüleġü küčü ögüleġe.
sentences.l: Than-whom more strength gave?
sentences.i: Than whom did they give more strength?
sentences.n: The second question, parallel to the first (ögüleġe marks no person; 'they' in `i` carries over Boγ̇orču, Muqali and the others from the first question, which is my reading): küčü 'strength' (Ming 氣力) and ög- 'give' (Ming 與來). The Ming write 氣力 as 'effort, labour', so 'gave strength' is 'gave of their effort'.

sentences.t: Sojurγal ögdeküj-e bi jaγ̇un dutaγ̇u tusa ese boluluγ̇a;
sentences.l: Favour to-the-to-be-given, I, what lacking service not did?
sentences.i: When favour is to be given, as for me, what service was lacking that I did not do?
sentences.n: Hard sentence; the words are plain but their joins are uncertain. Sojurγal ögdeküj-e is 'to (one) to be given favour': ög- 'give' + the passive -de- + the participle -kü + a linking j + dative -e (Ming 可與的行); bi 'I' follows it; a dative on a participle may mean 'when …' or 'to the one who …', and I take it as 'when favour is to be given', with bi the subject of the next clause. jaγ̇un dutaγ̇u tusa is 'what-lacking service' (dutaγ̇u 'lacking', Ming 缺少); ese boluluγ̇a is 'did (it) not become?' with the interrogative past (Ming 不曾做來麽). So: what service was wanting that I did not supply?

morph.gloss: favour, grace, bounty (from sojurγa- 'to show favour') [恩賜]

sentences.t: jaγ̇un dutaγ̇u küčü ese ögüleġe bi.
sentences.l: What lacking strength not gave I.
sentences.i: What strength was lacking that I did not give?
sentences.n: The parallel to the last: jaγ̇un dutaγ̇u küčü 'what-lacking strength', ese ögüleġe bi 'I did not give' (Ming 不曾與了來 我). Here the Ming add no 麽, but the sense is the same rhetorical question.

sentences.t: Ölegeitei büküi-eče ündür bosoγa-dur čin-u eriġün-dür edüi saqal urγutala ösčü öġere ese sedkibe-že bi.
sentences.l: Cradle-having being-from, high threshold-at your chin-at this-much beard sprouting-until growing, otherwise not thought I.
sentences.i: From the time I was in the cradle, growing up at your high threshold until this much beard sprouted on my chin, I never thought of anything else.
sentences.n: Ölegeitei is ölegei 'cradle' + -tei 'having', and the Ming add 裏 'in': 'in the cradle'. büküi-eče is 'from the being' (Ming 有的時行, 'from the time of being'). The threshold is the sill of the ruler's tent (bosoγa-dur čin-u, 'at your threshold', Ming 你的); eriġün-dür is 'on the chin' (Ming 下頷裏), and edüi saqal 'this much beard' (Ming 這些 髯), a gesture the reader does not see. urγutala is urγu- 'sprout' (stem inferred from the Ming 出來) + -tala 'until'. sedkibe-že: sedki- 'think' + past -be + emphatic -že (Ming 也者). öġere ese sedkibe 'did not think otherwise'.

morph.gloss: to sprout, grow out (stem inferred from the Ming 出來) [直到出來]

sentences.t: Ala-dur šiġegte-eče altan bosoγa-dur čin-u ažu
sentences.l: Fork-of-the-legs-in, chamber-pot-from, golden threshold-at your dwelling,
sentences.i: From the leg-fork, from the chamber-pot (that is, from earliest infancy), living at your golden threshold,
sentences.n: ala-dur is 'in the fork' (ala, Ming 腿叉 'crotch', the fork of the legs) and šiġegte-eče 'from the chamber-pot' (Ming 尿壺行): two images of earliest infancy, the child carried astride and the child in need of a pot. The reading is uncertain; the Ming are the only guide, and `i` keeps the two images and gives the sense in brackets. Then 'living at your golden threshold' (altan bosoγa-dur čin-u ažu, Ming 金門限裏你的住着). The long sentence is cut here into two units (257–262, 263–271); it closes with 'did not step wrongly' and bi.

morph.gloss: fork of the legs, crotch [腿叉]
chamber-pot (stem uncertain; Ming 尿壺) [尿壺]

sentences.t: aman-dur saqal edüi urγutala ösčü alžiγ̇as ese gedkibe-že bi.
sentences.l: Mouth-on beard this-much sprouting-until growing, error not trod I.
sentences.i: until this much beard grew out on my mouth, I never took a wrong step.
sentences.n: aman-dur 'on the mouth' (Ming 口裏); the beard is on the mouth and chin, so the two beard lines are the same boast in two forms. alžiγ̇as is 'error, going astray' (Ming 差). gedkibe-že is gedki- 'tread, step' (stem inferred from the Ming 踏) + past -be + emphatic -že, so alžiγ̇as ese gedkibe is 'did not tread on error', and the reader should keep the foot picture. Continues the previous unit.

morph.gloss: to sprout, grow out (stem inferred from the Ming 出來) [直到出來]
to tread, step (stem inferred from the Ming 踏) [踏了]

sentences.t: Köl-dür(i)-jen kebteġülžü köġüčilen ösgebe-že.
sentences.l: Own-foot-at making-lie-down, son-as raised.
sentences.i: I was made to lie at his own feet and brought up as a son.
sentences.n: No subject, and no object: 'me' is carried over from the next sentence's Nama-ji. The reflexive -jen (Ming 自的行, 'one's own') points back to the unnamed person who raised him; köl-dür(i)-jen is 'at his own foot', the (i) Shiratori's. kebteġülžü is kebte- 'lie down' + causative -ġül- + converb. köġüčilen is köġü 'son' + probably -čila- 'make into, treat as' + converb -n (Ming 做兒, 'make a son'); `i` gives 'as a son'. ösgebe is ös- 'grow' + causative -ge- + past -be, 'raised' (Ming 敎長了). That the 'son' and 'younger brother' clauses (next unit) name two different people is likely, not stated.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at (the (i) after it is Shiratori's linking vowel)

sentences.t: Nama-ji dergede-ġen kebteġülžü deġüčilen ösgebe-že.
sentences.l: Me (obj.) own-side-at making-lie-down, younger-brother-as raised.
sentences.i: And I was made to lie at his own side and brought up as a younger brother.
sentences.n: Same frame as the last unit. Nama-ji is bi 'I' on its oblique stem nama- + the accusative -ji (Ming 我行). dergede-ġen is 'at one's own side' (Ming 根前自的行), the reflexive -ġen. deġüčilen is deġü 'younger brother' + the same -čilen; Ming 做第 is the edition's slip for 做弟.

sentences.t: Nama-ji edöġe na-da ambar sojurγal ögümü" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Me (obj.) now, to-me what favour giving?” he-said.
sentences.i: Now, as for me, what favour is given to me?” he said.
sentences.n: Shiratori closes the speech on ögümü. Nama-ji and na-da are both 'me' (accusative, then dative), the first a topic: 'as for me'. ambar sojurγal is 'what favour' (Ming 甚麽 恩賜; ambar is uncertain, a word not found elsewhere, read from the Ming). ögümü is ög- 'give' + a linking vowel + -mü, which I take as a present or interrogative ending (Ming 與有, 'is given'). keġežüġüi is keġe- 'say' + the past -žüġüi.

morph.gloss: what, something (sense uncertain; Ming 甚麽) [甚麽]
favour, grace, bounty (from sojurγa- 'to show favour') [恩賜]

sentences.t: Tere üge-dür Čiṅgis Qaγan Šigi-Qutuqu-da ügülerün:
sentences.l: That word-in Čiṅgis Qaγan Šigi-Qutuqu-to saying:
sentences.i: In reply to those words, Chinggis Qahan said to Shigi-Qutuqu:
sentences.n: tere üge-dür is 'in that word' (Ming 那言語裏), here 'in answer to that speech'. The speaker is now named: Chinggis. ügülerün 'saying' with the colon opens his reply.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Žirγoduγ̇ar deġü busu-u či.
sentences.l: “Sixth younger-brother not-is-it you?
sentences.i: “Are you not the sixth younger brother?
sentences.n: Opening quote on Žirγoduγ̇ar is Shiratori's; his closing mark is on aldatuγai (313). Žirγoduγ̇ar is the ordinal 'sixth' (Ming 第六). busu-u is busu 'is not' + the interrogative -u (Ming 不是有麽), 'is it not so?'. I do not know what the six counts; the text does not say, and the Ming give only 第六.

sentences.t: Oroču deġü-deġen čima-da sojurγal deġü-ner-ün qubi-ijar qubilaldu.
sentences.l: Late-born own-younger-brother-to you-to favour, younger-brothers' share-according-to share-out.
sentences.i: To you, my own late-born younger brother, favour: share it out together, according to the portion of the younger brothers.
sentences.n: Oroču is 'late-born' (Ming 晩生的) and deġü-deġen 'to one's own younger brother', the reflexive pointing back to the speaker, Chinggis; čima-da is 'to you'. qubi-ijar is qubi 'share, portion' + the instrumental -ijar 'by, according to' (Ming 依着). qubilaldu is qubila- 'divide' + -ldu, which I read as 'among themselves' with the bare stem as imperative (Ming 分); the whole sentence is uncertain in its joins: either the favour is shared as the younger brothers' portion, or the brother is to share in the favours as a younger brother. The Ming have the first order.

morph.gloss: late-born, born last (Ming 晩生的) [晩生的]
dative-locative with reflexive-possessive: 'to one's own' [自的行]
favour, grace, bounty (from sojurγa- 'to show favour') [恩賜]
together, mutually (reciprocal; the bare stem is the imperative; uncertain)

sentences.t: Basa tusas-un čin-u tula jesün aldal- dür bu aldatuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Again, services' your because-of, nine penalty-in not let-be-fined,” saying, decree it-became.
sentences.i: Again, in return for your services, you shall not be punished for nine offences.” So it was decreed.
sentences.n: Closes Chinggis's speech (his quote mark is on aldatuγai). tusas-un is tusa 'service' + plural -s + genitive -un (Ming 恩每的); čin-u tula, 'your because-of' (Ming 你的 上頭). jesün aldal- dür is 'in nine penalties': the edition breaks aldal-/dür across a line, and the packet counts it as two words; the Ming 罰 … 裏 'in the fine'. bu aldatuγai is a negative optative, 'let (him) not be fined' (alda- 'incur a fine' + -tuγai; Ming 休罰者); the person is not marked, and 'you' is my reading. Nine is the number of offences forgiven (Ming 九次, 'nine times'). čin-u tula follows the house rendering of tula, 'in return for'.

morph.gloss: because of, for the sake of [上頭]
fault, penalty, fine (the hyphen is the line-break; -dür follows) [罰]
dative-locative: in (the second half of the broken word) [裏]
to incur a penalty, to offend (Ming 罰)

sentences.t: "Müṅke teṅgeri-de igeġegdežü gür ulus-i žügleġülžü
sentences.l: Eternal Heaven-by being-helped, whole people (obj.) making-right,
sentences.i: “Protected and helped by Eternal Heaven, and setting the whole people right,
sentences.n: Shiratori opens a new quotation on Müṅke. A converb chain with no main verb until ög (346), broken here into units of a few clauses each (317–322, 323–329, 330–336, 337–346). Heaven is the doer of a passive: teṅgeri-de, 'by Heaven' (Ming 行), with igeġegdežü, 'being helped, protected' (Ming 被護助着; the stem igeġe- is inferred). gür is 'all, whole' (Ming 普), not the title Gür of the glossary; I take it as the adjective. žügleġülžü is žügle- 'set right' (stem inferred from the Ming 正) + causative -ġül- + -žü. The speaker is Chinggis.

morph.gloss: Heaven, the sky as a power [天]
dative-locative: 'by', the doer of a passive [行]
to protect, help (stem inferred from the Ming 護助)
to set right, put in order (stem inferred from the Ming 正; from žüg 'direction')

sentences.t: büküi-dür či üžekü-jin nidün sonosqu-jin čikin bolžu
sentences.l: Being-when, you seeing's eye, hearing's ear becoming,
sentences.i: while that is so, you becoming the eye that sees and the ear that hears,
sentences.n: büküi-dür is bü- 'be' + the participle -küi + dative-locative -dür, 'while being' (Ming 有 時). üžekü-jin nidün is 'the seeing's eye', 'the eye that sees', and sonosqu-jin čikin 'the hearing's ear' (Ming 見的眼, 聽的耳): the ruler's eyes and ears, a counsellor and watcher. The possessor stands first: the genitive -jin is the participle's.

sentences.t: gür ulus-i eke-de bidan-a deġü-ner-e köġüd-te qubi
sentences.l: Whole people (obj.) to-mother to-us to-younger-brothers to-sons share,
sentences.i: the whole people, as shares to mother, to us, to the younger brothers, to the sons,
sentences.n: Now the substance of the order, a division of the people as shares (qubi, Ming 分子). eke-de 'to the mother', bidan-a 'to us' (bida is the inclusive 'we', Ming 咱), deġü-ner-e 'to the younger brothers' (plural -ner), köġüd-te 'to the sons' (köġü + plural -d + dative -te): each with the dative-locative (Ming 行). The recipients are listed as mother, 'us' (the speaker's own side), the younger brothers and the sons; the verb ög 'give' comes at the end of the chain, in the next unit.

sentences.t: irgen-ü nere-ġer isgeitü joγ̇urγatan-i iričeġülžü qabdasun eġüdeten-i qaγačaγ̇ulžu qubilažu ög.
sentences.l: People's name-by felt-having tent-wall-havers (obj.) dividing, plank door-havers (obj.) separating, sharing, give.
sentences.i: by the names of the peoples, setting apart the felt-tent folk, separating off the board-door folk, and sharing them out: give them.
sentences.n: irgen-ü nere-ġer is 'by the people's name' (nere-ġer, instrumental, Ming 名依着). isgeitü joγ̇urγatan-i is 'the felt-having, wall-havers (obj.)': isgei is felt (as hisgei above) and joγ̇urγa the tent-skirt (toγ̇urγa above, with the other first letter); -tü, -tan 'having' (Ming 有的 / 有的每). qabdasun eġüdeten-i is 'board-having, door-havers' (Ming 板 門有的每), which, set against the felt tents, I take for the forest peoples of the board-door dwellings (compare hoi-in irgen in §202); that is my reading. iričeġülžü 'setting apart' (Ming 分着; the stem is the glossary's hiriče-, 'part, separate') and qaγačaγ̇ulžu 'separating' and qubilažu 'sharing out' are the three converbs; ög is the bare imperative 'give!'.

morph.gloss: tent-wall, tent-skirt (a variant of toγ̇urγa) [帳墻]
to part, separate (printed iriče-; as hiriče- in the glossary; Ming 分) [分着]

sentences.t: Ken ber čin-u üge buši bu bolγatiγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Anyone your word otherwise not let-make,” saying, decree it-became.
sentences.i: Let no one make your word otherwise.” So it was decreed.
sentences.n: Ken ber is 'anyone, whoever' (ber 'even, also', Ming 也), which with bu 'do not' means 'no one'. buši is 'other, otherwise' (Ming 別). bolγatiγai is bol- 'become' + causative -γa- + optative -tiγai (Ming 做者), 'let (him) make' ; so 'make your word otherwise', i.e. 'alter it'. Closes the quote opened at Müṅke (317), printed on bolγatiγai.

sentences.t: "Basa Šigi-Qutuqu-ji gür ulus-un qulaγai-ji keseġüžü qudal-i moγaγ̇ažu
sentences.l: “Again, Šigi-Qutuqu (obj.), whole people's thieves (obj.) punishing, lies (obj.) clearing-up,
sentences.i: “Again: Shigi-Qutuqu is to punish the thieves of the whole people and expose lies;
sentences.n: A new decree, opened on Basa and closed on aldaγ̇ul (370); it is cut into two units here, and the rest of the sentence (keġen … tüšibe, 371–375) stands outside the quotation. Šigi-Qutuqu-ji is accusative because he is the object of tüšibe at the end: 'appointed Šigi-Qutuqu'; I carry the sense into the quotation as 'Shigi-Qutuqu is to'. qulaγai-ji 'thief (obj.)'; keseġüžü is 'punishing, admonishing' (Ming 懲戒着; the stem is uncertain). qudal-i moγaγ̇ažu is 'lies (obj.), making white' (Ming 謊 白着); I take 'exposing lies' but the stem moγaγ̇a- is uncertain.

morph.gloss: to punish, admonish (stem uncertain; Ming 懲戒)
to make clear, expose (stem uncertain; Ming 白)

sentences.t: üküġüldekün josutan-i üküġül; aldaγ̇uldaqun josutan-i aldaγ̇ul"
sentences.l: To-be-put-to-death right-havers (obj.) cause-to-die; fine-deserving right-havers (obj.) cause-to-be-fined,”
sentences.i: put to death those who by law deserve death, and fine those who by law deserve a fine.”
sentences.n: üküġüldekün is ük- 'die' + causative -ġül- + -dekün (passive -de- + future participle -kün), 'one who is to be …ed' (Ming 可敎死的); josutan-i is josu(n) 'law, right' + -tan 'having' + accusative (Ming 理有的每行), 'those with right' i.e. those who by the law deserve it. üküġül and aldaγ̇ul are the bare causative stems, imperatives: 'cause (them) to die', 'cause (them) to be fined'. aldaγ̇uldaqun 'one who is to be fined' (Ming 可罰的). Shiratori's closing quote mark is on aldaγ̇ul.

morph.gloss: passive -de- + future participle -kün: 'one who is to be …ed' [可 … 的]
to incur a penalty, to offend (Ming 罰)
passive -da- + future participle -qun: 'one who is to be …ed' [可 … 的]
to incur a penalty, to offend [敎罰]

sentences.t: keġen gür deġere-jin žarγu tüšibe.
sentences.l: Saying, whole above's judge appointed.
sentences.i: So he appointed him supreme judge over all.
sentences.n: keġen closes the quotation and tüšibe 'appointed' (Ming 委付了) takes up Šigi-Qutuqu-ji from 358 as its object. žarγu is 'judging, a judge's office' (Ming 斷事, 'deciding affairs'); gür deġere-jin žarγu is 'the over-all's judge', which I read as 'judge over all', highest of them. An office of supreme judge; the Ming give no more.

morph.gloss: judgement, the office of judge (Ming 斷事, 'deciding affairs') [斷事]

sentences.t: "Basa gür irgen-ü qubi qubilaγsan-i žarγu žarγulaγsan-i
sentences.l: “Again, whole people's share-apportioned (obj.), judgement-judged (obj.),
sentences.i: “Again: the shares of the whole people that have been apportioned, the judgments that have been given,
sentences.n: A third decree, opened on Basa and closed on boltuγai (405). qubilaγsan-i and žarγulaγsan-i are past participles in -γsan with the accusative -i (Ming 分了的 行, 斷了的 行): 'what has been apportioned', 'what has been judged'; they are the objects of the whole sentence and of the final jeġüdge- 'alter'. žarγula- is 'to judge' (from žarγu).

morph.gloss: accusative: object marker [分了的 行]
judgement, the office of judge (Ming 斷事) [斷事]
accusative: object marker [斷了的 行]

sentences.t: kökö debter bičig bičižü debterležü
sentences.l: Blue register writing having-written, having-registered,
sentences.i: writing them in the blue register and entering them,
sentences.n: kökö debter bičig, 'blue register, writing' (Ming 靑 冊 文書): the Blue Register is the Mongol records book. debter is a loanword, 'notebook, register' (Ming 冊); debterležü is debterle- 'to register' + converb. The subject is again unstated; the converb chain continues over the next two units.

morph.gloss: to register in a book [造册着]

sentences.t: uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele Sigi-Qutoqu-jin na-dur ejetüžü josulažu
sentences.l: Descendants' descendants-to until, Šigi-Qutuqu's me-with having-consulted, having-deliberated,
sentences.i: and, down to the descendants of descendants, with Shigi-Qutuqu consulting me and settling it,
sentences.n: uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele is 'to the offspring of the offspring, until' (Ming 子孫的子孫行直到): for ever. The edition prints Sigi-Qutoqu-jin (no caron, o for u) here: a slip, not a different man; the genitive -jin goes with the consultation, and na-dur 'to me, with me' (Ming 我行) completes it: 'Shigi-Qutuqu's, with me, consulting'. ejetüžü 'consulting' (stem inferred from the Ming 商量) and josulažu 'deliberating, judging by right' (from josu; Ming 議擬). A genitive on the one who consults is unusual, so the joining is uncertain.

morph.gloss: Shigi-Qutuqu, a man's name (printed Sigi-Qutoqu) [人名]
to consult, deliberate (stem inferred from the Ming 商量)
to deliberate, decide by right (from josu 'law, right'; Ming 議擬)

sentences.t: kökö bičig čaγaγ̇an čaγ̇alsun-dur debterlegsen-i bu jeġüdgetüġei.
sentences.l: Blue writing white paper-on registered (obj.) not let-be-altered.
sentences.i: what is entered in blue writing on white paper shall not be altered.
sentences.n: kökö bičig čaγaγ̇an čaγ̇alsun-dur is 'blue writing on white paper' (Ming 靑文書 白紙行); debterlegsen-i is 'what has been registered (obj.)' (Ming 造冊來行). The main verb at last: bu jeġüdgetüġei, 'let it not be altered' (jeġüdge- 'to change, alter', Ming 更改; -tüġei the optative). The accusative -i makes what was registered the object of the alteration.

sentences.t: Jeġüdgekün haran aldaltan boltuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Altering person fine-having let-be,” saying, decree it-became.
sentences.i: Whoever alters it shall be liable to a fine.” So it was decreed.
sentences.n: jeġüdgekün haran is 'the altering person' (jeġüdge- + -kün participle; haran 'person, people', Ming 人). aldaltan is aldal 'fine, penalty' + -tan 'having' (Ming 罰有的): 'fine-having', i.e. liable. boltuγai is the optative 'let (him) be' (Ming 做者). Closes the quotation opened at Basa (376); Shiratori's mark is on boltuγai.

sentences.t: Šigi-Qutuqu ügülerün:
sentences.l: Šigi-Qutuqu saying:
sentences.i: Shigi-Qutuqu said:
sentences.n: Shigi-Qutuqu replies to the decree. ügülerün, 'saying', and the colon.

sentences.t: "Min-u metü oroču deġü sačaγ̇u deṅgečen qubi ker abqu.
sentences.l: “My like late-born younger-brother alike level share how take?
sentences.i: “How is a late-born younger brother like me to take a share the same and equal?
sentences.n: Shiratori opens a quote on Min-u. min-u is bi 'I' on its genitive stem min- + -u, 'my' (Ming 我的) and metü is 'like, as': 'a late-born younger brother like me' (Ming 我的般 晩生的弟). sačaγ̇u deṅgečen is 'alike, level' (Ming 一般 齊等): an equal share. ker abqu 'how take' (Ming 怎生 要): the question is how such a younger brother is to take an equal share ('how is one to take', not 'how can one'); abqu is ab- 'take' + the participle -qu.

sentences.t: Sojurγaγ̇asu široγ̇ai joγ̇urγatu balaγasun-ača ögkü-ji Qaγan-(n)u sojurγal medetügei" keġen öčižüġü.
sentences.l: Favour-if-showing, earth wall-having town-from giving (obj.), Qaγan's favour let-know,” saying, he-petitioned.
sentences.i: If you show favour, in giving from the earth-walled towns, let the Qahan's favour be known,” he petitioned.
sentences.n: Shiratori's closing quote is on medetügei. The joins are uncertain. sojurγaγ̇asu is sojurγa- 'show favour' + the conditional -γ̇asu, 'if (he) shows favour' (Ming 恩賜呵). široγ̇ai joγ̇urγatu balaγasun-ača is 'earth, wall-having towns-from' (Ming 土 墻有的 (城)子每處): the walled, settled towns, set against the felt tents; ögkü-ji is ög- 'give' + participle -kü + accusative -ji (Ming 與的行), 'the giving'. Qaγan-(n)u sojurγal medetügei, 'let the Qahan's favour be known' (mede- 'know' + the third-person optative; who is to know is not stated). The subject of öčižüġü is Šigi-Qutuqu: öči- 'say to a superior, petition' (Ming 奏, 'memorialize'; stem inferred), -žüġü a short past.

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace (Ming 恩賜)
favour, grace, bounty (from sojurγa- 'to show favour') [恩賜]
to petition, say to a superior (stem inferred from the Ming 奏 'memorialize') [奏了]

sentences.t: Ene üge-dür "öġer-ün beje-ben či čaγlaba; či mede" keġebe.
sentences.l: This word-in, “own's body-own you weighed; you know,” he-said.
sentences.i: In reply to these words he said, “You have weighed your own self; you know.”
sentences.n: A short, hard answer, and the speaker is not named; given the reply to a petition, it is Chinggis. Shiratori opens a quote on öġer-ün. öġer-ün beje-ben is 'of oneself, one's own body' (Ming 自己的身子自的行), the reflexive -ben; čaγlaba is čaγla- 'weigh, judge' (Ming 斟酌) + past -ba, and mede is the bare imperative of mede- 'know': 'you have taken your own measure, you decide' is the sense I take, but 'you know' may rather be 'know it!'. The weight falls on či, 'you'. The Ming 行 on öġer-ün beje-ben marks it as what is weighed, so `i` has 'weighed your own self', not 'weighed it for yourself'.

sentences.t: Šigi-Qutuqu öġer(i)-jen tein sojurγaγ̇ulun baražu
sentences.l: Šigi-Qutuqu own-to thus favour-causing-to-be-shown, having-finished,
sentences.i: When Shigi-Qutuqu had thus had favour shown to himself,
sentences.n: The aftermath, cut in two (439–443, 444–449). öġer(i)-jen is 'his own' (Ming 自己(自的)行): öġer 'own' with the reflexive -jen, the (i) Shiratori's. tein is 'so, thus' (Ming 那般). sojurγaγ̇ulun is sojurγa- 'show favour' + -γ̇ul- + converb -n, with the Ming 恩賜 only: 'having had favour shown', I take the causative as passive-like (uncertain). baražu 'finishing' (Ming 了着). The sense: he had favour shown to himself on those terms; what the favour was is not said.

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace (Ming 恩賜) [恩賜]

sentences.t: γarču Boγ̇orču, Muqali-tan nojad-i urižu oroγ̇ulžuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Going-out, Boγ̇orču, Muqali and-others nobles (obj.) calling, making-enter.
sentences.i: he went out, called Bo'orchu, Muqali and the other lords, and brought them in.
sentences.n: The thread of the opening of the section: Šigi-Qutuqu had been sent to fetch the lords (208–214) and now does so. γarču is γar- 'go out' + converb -ču (Ming 出着); urižu 'calling' (Ming 喚着); oroγ̇ulžuγ̇u is oro- 'enter' + causative -γ̇ul- + the past -žuγ̇u, 'made (them) enter' (Ming 敎入來了, 'caused to come in'). The accusative nojad-i governs both verbs. Subject is still Shigi-Qutuqu.
